newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Punjab cotton prices gain on low supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian Punjab cotton prices gain on low supply.

text.p: Indian Punjab cotton prices on Tuesday gained while Gujarat varieties fell, dealers said.
Punjab varieties extended gains on the back of dwindling arrivals at producing centres coupled with a shortage of ready stock.

In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose by 20/25 rupees at 1,800/1,880 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 rose by 10 rupees at 2,050/2,060 rupees per maund and Bengal-deshi rose by five rupees at 1,005/1,035 rupees per maund.
Gujarat varieties lost recent gains as local stockists unloaded stocks to book profits at a higher level ahead of the monsoon, one broker said.

Spot Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) fell by 100/300 rupees at 14,300/14,900 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton fell by 200 rupees at 13,200 rupees and Kala-ginned fell by 200 rupees at 12,900/13,000 rupees per candy.
